answer: A port authority can require each agent identity to post a copper bond that is locked for weeks before it may dock at the wharf, so a Sybil farm must fund every fake identity up front. Honest agents earn the bond back through verified work, while a flood of throwaway identities faces a spiral of rising costs: each new fake needs fresh capital, and slashing burns the bond of any identity caught copying or lying. Attackers pay linearly per identity while defenders verify cheaply.
